text: As the Patriots prepare to host the Pittsburgh Steelers for their home opener at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, September 20 at 1 PM ET, the team faces a significant challenge with wide receiver A.J. Brown heading to injured reserve after suffering a high ankle sprain in Week 1—a setback that will sideline him for at least four games and force other receivers to step into prominent roles in the offense. Head Coach Mike Vrabel addressed the situation during his Wednesday press conference, and analysts like Mike Reiss have been examining which Patriots receivers will need to pick up the slack in Brown's absence as Drake Maye looks to bounce back following the team's Week 1 performance. Off the field, Patriots owner Robert Kraft demonstrated the organization's commitment to its values by removing Macklemore as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium, citing "a history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community." Meanwhile, Maye and his wife Ann Michael made headlines for their own generosity, purchasing Amazon classroom wish lists for over 50 teachers and support staff at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence, Rhode Island, as part of a back-to-school initiative.
